title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-06-08

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy first set (Dancin', He Was a Friend of Mine, China Cat → New Potato) with solid recording quality despite minor pitch quirks.
ai_review.review: The recording is a well‑preserved soundboard source that sounds crisp and balanced, though listeners note a slight speed/pitch issue on “Dancing in the Street” and occasional low‑level mic for Wayne. Musically the show shines in the first set – a smoking Dancin', gorgeous “He Was a Friend of Mine,” and an unforgettable China Cat → New Potato sequence – while the second set is more uneven, with “Lovelight” cited as weak but still offering highlights like Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One → Cosmic Charlie.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4‑5 stars and praise the performance, especially the first set, while a few note second‑set flaws and minor recording pitch issues; the balance yields an overall strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp soundboard mix with clear instrument separation. Minor speed/pitch anomalies on “Dancing in the Street” need slight correction; one comment about Wayne's vocal mic being low, but overall clean and listenable.

standout_songs: He Was a Friend of Mine
China Cat Sunflower → New Potato Caboose
Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One → Cosmic Charlie
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set flows tightly with seamless transitions and high energy; second set is more fragmented due to dosing, but still contains a strong mid‑set suite.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar tone praised as “perfect” and “far‑away weeping”; his vocal cracks noted on Dancin' outro; sat out briefly during the dosed second set.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass described as “crazy,” “blazing,” with unique chord work and a memorable solo on New Potato; praised for “Phil bombs.”
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob’s harmonies highlighted as sweet and supportive, especially on “He Was a Friend of Mine.”
